text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Japan will give Romania a $175 million credit to build a container terminal in the Black Sea port of Constanta, the paper says.
- South Korea's Daewoo Corporation plans to build $100 million car parts factory, it says.
- SNCFR railway authority sold 25,000 tonnes of scrap iron to Duferco SA of Switzerland.
- The government decided to allot 550 billion lei in credits for seasonal farm works.
- Locomotive maker Electroputere Craiova plans to sign cooperation agreement with Siemens AG of Germany to build 120 train engines.
- Subsidies given by the former leftist government to state-run animal farms had been allegedly misused by officials in charge of the sector, the paper says.
- A group of U.S. companies plan to invest $170 million in Romania's farming sector, the paper quotes agriculture minister Dan Gavrilescu as saying.
- Inflation amunted to 18.8 percent in February.
- The leu-dollar convertibility will be achieved "gradually but fast", the paper quotes central bank governor Mugur Isarescu as saying during a visit to Budapest.
